categoryName: Staples & flours (atta, rice, sooji, poha, maida, besan)

skuLines.line: Chakki whole wheat atta — economy tier
skuLines.examples: NAFED Bharat Atta 10kg, Patanjali Chakki Atta, local Solan/Nahan mill brand, store private label
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; dips in Dec-Jan and May-Jun school vacations when student/canteen pull collapses
skuLines.notes: Bharat Atta's ₹30/kg MRP is the price anchor everyone compares against. Atta keeps only 1-2 months at room temperature and Baru Sahib monsoon humidity crosses 80% — buy 3-4 week lots Jul-Sep, never a monsoon buffer. Heaviest freight item in the store.

skuLines.line: Chakki whole wheat atta — mainstream national brand
skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Atta, Fortune Chakki Fresh, Pillsbury Chakki Fresh, Shakti Bhog
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes at Gurpurabs (karah prasad is equal parts atta, ghee, sugar)
skuLines.notes: The single largest ₹ line in the category. 1 kg/2 kg exists for hostel rooms and top-ups, not for families — stock both ends or the top-up sale leaks. Pack date matters more than MRP here.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Select Sharbati, Rajdhani Sharbati, Shakti Bhog Select, 24 Mantra Organic Wheat Atta
skuLines.notes: Faculty and senior staff households are the buyers. One facing is enough — but its absence is exactly the ₹ that leaks to a Solan/Nahan trip.

skuLines.line: Loose / freshly ground chakki atta by weight
skuLines.examples: Own in-store chakki output, local Rajgarh mill loose atta, unbranded sabut-gehun grind
skuLines.packSizes: Sold by weight — 1 kg to 10 kg, customer's own container
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; heaviest Jul-Sep when packed atta spoils fastest
skuLines.notes: Highest-margin line in the whole category and the correct answer to hill flour spoilage — you hold whole grain, not flour. Repacking or selling loose needs an FSSAI licence and a Legal-Metrology-verified scale; declarations required if you pre-pack into your own bags.

skuLines.line: Sabut gehun (whole wheat grain) for own grinding
skuLines.examples: Local HP/Punjab wheat, MP Sharbati sabut gehun, cleaned mill-grade wheat
skuLines.seasonality: Bulk household buying Apr-Jun right after the wheat harvest, before monsoon
skuLines.notes: The hill hedge: grain survives a landslide-blocked road and a wet month, flour does not. Sell alongside grinding service and pest-proof storage tins. Needs pallets off the floor and neem/bay-leaf sachets.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Multigrain, Tata Sampann Multigrain, Patanjali Multigrain, Fortune Multigrain
skuLines.notes: Typically wheat + soya + chana + oats + maize + psyllium. Shorter shelf life than plain atta because of the oil-bearing grains — rotate faster in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Atta with High Protein (launched Sep 2025), Tata Simply Better, Rebalance high-protein atta
skuLines.notes: Newest real shelf tier in Indian atta. University-age gym cohort and health-aware faculty buy it; a school-child household will not. One SKU, one facing.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Sugar Release Control Atta, Tata Sampann Diabetes-friendly blends, Diabexy atta
skuLines.notes: 5,000 residents includes ageing staff and retired-quarters elderly with no alternative retailer within 30-50 km — this is a medical-necessity line, not a wellness fad. Stock small, never go out of stock.

skuLines.line: Fortified atta (+F, iron / folic acid / B12)
skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Nature's Super Foods fortified variants, state-programme fortified atta, +F-marked mill atta
skuLines.notes: Relevant for a residential school population with anaemia risk. Note the 2026 reversal: GoI suspended FRK fortified-RICE distribution in Feb 2026 over storage degradation, while fortified-ATTA programmes kept expanding — so lead with atta, not rice, on fortification claims.

skuLines.line: Everyday non-basmati raw rice (permal / PR-11 / PR-14 / medium grain)
skuLines.examples: Local Punjab permal, PR-126 mill rice, store private label 'daily rice', Whole Farm everyday rice
skuLines.packSizes: 5 kg, 10 kg, 25 kg bag; loose by weight
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; household bulk buying Nov-Dec after the kharif crop
skuLines.notes: The workhorse rice — most residents eat this, not basmati. Rice is far more monsoon-tolerant than flour, so this is the line you can legitimately buffer 6-8 weeks against a blocked hill road.

skuLines.examples: NAFED Bharat Rice 5kg/10kg, NCCF/Kendriya Bhandar Bharat Rice
skuLines.notes: Phase-II MRP is ₹34/kg. Availability is programme-dependent and lumpy; treat as an opportunistic value line, never as your base rice.

skuLines.examples: Daawat Rozana Super, Fortune Rozana Gold, India Gate Feast Rozana, Kohinoor Everyday
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; uplift at festivals and family visits
skuLines.notes: The bridge SKU between daily rice and premium basmati; sells more units than premium basmati at any hill outlet.

skuLines.examples: India Gate Classic, Daawat Devaaya, Kohinoor Super Silver, Lal Qilla
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp spikes at Gurpurabs, Diwali, weddings, parents' visiting days and convocation
skuLines.notes: Also the default gift/hospitality pack. Ages well — the one staple where slow turns do not hurt quality.

skuLines.examples: India Gate Golden Sella, Daawat Biryani Basmati Sella, Kohinoor Sella
skuLines.notes: Non-sticky and forgiving in a large degh — this is what canteens and langar kitchens actually want for biryani/pulao at scale. Sell the 25 kg through the institutional counter.

skuLines.examples: bb Royal Sona Masoori, Maharaja Ponni, Daawat Kolam, Karnataka Ponni
skuLines.seasonality: Follows the academic calendar — falls to near-zero in vacation months
skuLines.notes: Eternal University and Akal Academy draw students and faculty from South India and the East who will not eat north-Indian permal daily. Small but non-substitutable cohort; one or two SKUs prevent a guaranteed off-campus leak.

skuLines.examples: Pavizham/Nirapara idli rice, bb Royal Idli Rice, Anil parboiled rice
skuLines.notes: Pair it with idli rava and urad — selling one without the others makes the line dead stock.

skuLines.examples: Loose broken rice, mill kanki, store-packed 'khichdi rice'
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; uplift in illness season and winter
skuLines.notes: Cheapest calorie in the store, and the standard base for baby khichdi, kheer and convalescent food. Loose sale carries kirana-grade margin, not rice-grade margin.

skuLines.line: Brown rice / red rice / low-GI rice
skuLines.examples: India Gate Brown Basmati, 24 Mantra Organic Red Rice, Daawat Brown Basmati
skuLines.notes: Bran-bearing, so it goes rancid in 4-6 months and much faster in a humid hill store. Keep one SKU, smallest pack, and watch the date.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Sooji, bb Royal Bombay Rava, Rajdhani Sooji, Fortune Sooji
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; strong spikes at every Gurpurab and religious function (sooji halwa / prasad)
skuLines.notes: At a Sikh institution the prasad and langar-sweet pull makes sooji behave like a festival SKU, not a breakfast SKU — forecast against the religious calendar, not the month.

skuLines.examples: Chiroti rava, fine sooji, bb Royal Fine Sooji, Meenakshi chiroti rava
skuLines.notes: Not interchangeable with coarse rava — fine goes into laddoo/kesari/halwa, coarse into upma. Substituting one for the other is the most common complaint in this sub-line.

skuLines.examples: bb Royal Idli Rava, Nirapara Idli Rava, Anil Idli Rava
skuLines.notes: Rice-based, not wheat — needed for quick idli without wet grinding, which suits hostel and small-quarter kitchens.

skuLines.line: Bansi rava / samba wheat rava (coarse wheat rava)
skuLines.examples: Bansi rava, samba godhumai rava, Meenakshi Bansi Rava
skuLines.notes: Regional-specific; only worth one facing while South Indian faculty are in residence.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Maida, Rajdhani Maida, bb Royal Maida, Pillsbury Maida
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; monsoon uplift (pakora/samosa) and festival sweets
skuLines.notes: Longest shelf life of any flour here (low oil, low bran) — the safest flour to hold through monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Mill 25 kg / 50 kg maida bag, Rajdhani institutional maida
skuLines.notes: Two canteens, a bakery habit and langar puri/bhature all pull from the same bag. Sell on quotation through the institutional counter, not off the POS shelf.

skuLines.examples: Whole Farm Premium Rice Flour, bb Royal Rice Flour, Nirapara Rice Powder
skuLines.notes: Double duty in Himachal: chilra/pathande and local rice breads, plus South Indian cooking and fry-coating. Cheap, fast-moving, forgiving.

skuLines.examples: Brown & Polson Corn Flour, Weikfield Corn Flour, Blue Bird, ararot powder
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; arrowroot spikes at fasting periods
skuLines.notes: Thickener for canteen gravies and Indo-Chinese; arrowroot doubles as a vrat-permitted starch. Very long shelf life, negligible spoilage risk.

skuLines.examples: Rajdhani Besan, Tata Sampann Besan, Aashirvaad Besan, loose mill besan
skuLines.packSizes: 500 g, 1 kg, 5 kg; loose by weight
skuLines.seasonality: Big monsoon spike (pakora weather is most of Jul-Sep here), plus Diwali/Gurpurab sweets and winter kadhi
skuLines.notes: In a cold, wet hill township besan behaves like a seasonal hero, not a background staple. Oil-bearing — turns bitter in 3-4 months; buy short and often.

skuLines.examples: Tata Sampann Sattu, Bharat Sattu, Manna Sattu, local roasted-chana sattu
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks Apr-Jun (summer drink); low in winter
skuLines.notes: Bihar/UP/Jharkhand students treat it as a daily drink and a cheap protein — a cohort-specific must that a Punjab-centric buyer routinely skips.

skuLines.line: Chana atta / missi atta (whole bengal gram flour blend)
skuLines.examples: Rajdhani Chana Atta, Aashirvaad Missi Atta, Patanjali Chana Atta
skuLines.notes: The traditional low-GI roti for diabetics — often bought instead of an expensive branded 'diabetic atta'. Stock both and let price decide.

skuLines.examples: Nutrela Soya Atta, Patanjali Soya Atta, Fortune Soya Chunks flour
skuLines.notes: Blended into atta for protein. High oil content — shortest shelf life of the pulse flours, keep one small pack.

skuLines.examples: Rajdhani Makki Atta, Aashirvaad Makai Atta, local HP maize flour, loose makki
skuLines.seasonality: Hard winter peak Nov-Feb (makki di roti with sarson); thin in summer
skuLines.notes: Non-negotiable for a Punjabi-majority population in a cold place, and maize is grown locally in Himachal so a fresh local grind is available and preferred. Coarse maize flour goes rancid fast — do not carry summer stock into winter.

skuLines.examples: Goshudh Bajra Atta, Organic Tattva Bajra Flour, 24 Mantra Bajra Atta, loose bajra grind
skuLines.notes: Rancidity risk is the highest of the millet flours (6-8 weeks fresh). Stock seasonally, or sell the whole grain and grind on demand.

skuLines.examples: Tata Simply Better Sprouted Jowar Atta, Organic Tattva Jowar, KEW Miller Jowar
skuLines.notes: Naturally gluten-free and low-GI — the workhorse of the health-flour tier. Sells to the same buyer as diabetic atta.

skuLines.examples: Organic Tattva Ragi Flour, Manna Ragi, KEW Miller Ragi, local kodra grind
skuLines.notes: Triple pull unique to this location: kodra is a traditional Kullu/HP grain, ragi is the standard calcium/iron weaning flour for the babies of married staff, and it is the elderly's calcium staple. Highest-conviction millet line here.

skuLines.line: Jau / barley atta and barley grain
skuLines.examples: Radha Govind Organic Jau Atta, Dinesh Flour Mills Jau, local barley flour, sattu-jau
skuLines.seasonality: Winter and summer-sattu both; year-round baseline
skuLines.notes: Barley is one of the three grains Himachali traditional cooking is actually built on (with wheat and rice) and is grown locally — a hill store that skips jau is reading a plains planogram.

skuLines.examples: Manan Foods Kuttu Atta, Organic Mandya Kuttu, local ogla-phaphar grind
skuLines.seasonality: Navratri (Mar-Apr, Sep-Oct), Ekadashi, Shivratri — prices rise 15-35% in season; local bhaturu demand year-round
skuLines.notes: Uniquely dual-purpose at Baru Sahib: the pan-Indian fasting flour AND the traditional flour for Himachali bhaturu, which is made with wheat or buckwheat. Buy the season ahead; it is the one flour where a stock-out is unforgivable and a price rise is accepted. Food-safety history of adulterated/stale kuttu causing mass illness — buy branded, sealed, dated stock only.

skuLines.examples: Manan Foods Singhara Atta, Rajdhani Singhara, local vrat-atta packs
skuLines.seasonality: Navratri and fasting days only; near-zero otherwise
skuLines.notes: Pre-book against the festival calendar; dead weight the rest of the year. Pack date is critical — this is the flour most often sold stale.

skuLines.examples: Amwel Rajgira Atta, Organic Tattva Rajgira, 24 Mantra Amaranth Flour
skuLines.notes: Third fasting flour after kuttu and singhara; smallest pack only.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Multi Millet Mix, Earthen Story Multigrain Atta, Slurrp Farm millet atta
skuLines.notes: Post-millet-year mainstreaming; convenient for buyers who won't manage four separate flours. One SKU covers the whole millet-curious segment.

skuLines.line: Whole millet grains (ragi, bajra, jowar, kodo, samak)
skuLines.examples: Loose local millets, 24 Mantra whole millets, Dinesh Flour Mills whole grain
skuLines.notes: Whole grain solves the millet-flour rancidity problem outright — pair with the in-store chakki and you sell freshness instead of shelf life.

skuLines.examples: Tata Sampann Thick Poha, Fortune Indori Poha, bb Royal Thick Poha, loose thick poha
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; breakfast staple, steady through terms
skuLines.notes: Cheapest hot breakfast for 5,000 people and a canteen mainstay. Absorbs moisture fast — sealed packs beat loose in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: bb Royal Nylon Poha 500 g, Suraj Thin Poha, local nylon poha
skuLines.notes: Different job from thick poha — chivda, namkeen and instant snacking. Both facings needed.

skuLines.examples: Organic Tattva Red Rice Poha, Slurrp Farm brown poha, high-fibre poha
skuLines.notes: Health-tier poha; one facing.

skuLines.examples: Loose murmura, bb Royal Murmura, Haldiram's Murmura
skuLines.packSizes: 200 g, 500 g, 1 kg (very low density — bulky)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; bhel/snack uplift and religious offerings
skuLines.notes: High margin per rupee but terrible freight economics — huge volume, almost no weight, so it burns hill truck space. Buy from the nearest source, not a distant distributor.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Daliya, Tata Sampann Dalia, Rajdhani Dalia, loose dalia
skuLines.seasonality: Winter peak; year-round baseline; spikes in illness season
skuLines.notes: The single most-needed 'gentle food' in a township with babies, elderly and a school infirmary — porridge, khichdi, convalescent food. Cheap, long-lasting, no substitute available within 30-50 km.

skuLines.examples: bb Royal Sabudana, Rajdhani Sabudana, nylon sabudana, loose sago
skuLines.seasonality: Fasting periods (Navratri, Ekadashi, Shivratri); babies' kheer year-round
skuLines.notes: Very long shelf life and moisture-tolerant — one of the few staples safe to buffer heavily before monsoon.

skuLines.line: Samak / barnyard millet rice (vrat ke chawal)
skuLines.examples: Samak chawal, Manan Foods Vrat ke Chawal, barnyard millet
skuLines.notes: Stock only against the festival calendar; pre-book with the kuttu/singhara lot.

skuLines.examples: Bambino Vermicelli, MTR Roasted Vermicelli, Anil Vermicelli, seviyan for kheer
skuLines.notes: Sits with sooji in every Indian store's mental map and shares the same buyer trip. Fragile in transit on hill roads — expect breakage in the plain (non-roasted) packs.

skuLines.examples: Quaker Oats, Saffola Oats, Bagrry's Rolled Oats, True Elements
skuLines.notes: Buy plain, not flavoured, for this lane — flavoured sachets belong in breakfast/instant. Long shelf life, monsoon-tolerant if sealed.

skuLines.line: Sprouted ragi / sathu maavu baby porridge flour
skuLines.examples: Slurrp Farm Sprouted Ragi Cereal, Manna Health Mix, Healthy Panda Sathu Maavu, The Millet Store porridge mix
skuLines.notes: Married staff with babies and no shop within 30-50 km makes this a captive, high-loyalty line — a parent who finds it once returns monthly for two years. Sealed, dated, sprouted-and-roasted stock only; short shelf life (6-9 months) and humidity-sensitive. Distinct from tinned infant formula/cereal (different licence and category).

skuLines.examples: Rebalance GF atta, Amwel gluten-free flour, jowar-ragi-rice GF blends
skuLines.notes: Fastest-growing sub-segment in Indian flour (gluten-free high-protein atta ~USD 66.8 M in 2026, ~15% CAGR) but a tiny absolute base. Worth one SKU only if a known celiac household exists on campus — otherwise it expires on the shelf.

skuLines.examples: Aashirvaad Atta Institutional Pack 25 kg, mill 30 kg atta bag, Shakti Bhog bulk
skuLines.seasonality: Tracks the school/university term and langar calendar; collapses in vacations
skuLines.notes: Two canteens, a school mess and langar are the real volume behind this whole category. Quotation-and-indent business, not shelf business — thin margin, enormous turns, and it must never be priced off the retail shelf card. Store on pallets, FIFO, and do not hold more than ~3 weeks in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Mill permal 25 kg, Maharaja Ponni 26 kg, sella basmati 25 kg institutional
skuLines.notes: Unlike atta, rice bags tolerate a long hold — this is the right line to buffer 6-8 weeks against monsoon road closures on the 30-50 km hill approach.

skuLines.examples: Loose chokar, mill bran, bran-added atta
skuLines.notes: Two demand streams in a township: high-fibre rotis for diabetic/elderly households, and cattle feed for staff who keep a cow or buffalo. Near-zero cost if the store runs its own chakki — pure by-product margin.

trends2026: High-protein atta became a real shelf tier, not a claim: ITC launched Aashirvaad Atta with High Protein (wheat + soya + gram + oats) in Sep 2025 and the whole gluten-free high-protein atta sub-segment is valued around USD 66.8 M in 2026, growing ~15% CAGR to 2033.

Millet flours normalised post-millet-year: single-millet attas (ragi, jowar, bajra) and multi-millet blend attas (e.g. Aashirvaad Multi Millet Mix) now sit as standing SKUs in mainstream grocery rather than health-store specials, driven by low-GI positioning (millet mean GI ~55 vs milled rice ~72 and refined wheat ~74).

Fortification story flipped from rice to atta: GoI temporarily suspended FRK fortified-rice distribution through PDS in Feb 2026 after storage degradation of iron/folic acid/B12, while fortified whole-wheat atta (+F) programmes kept expanding through state partnerships — so 2026 nutrition messaging in staples leads with atta.

Subsidised Bharat brand reset the price floor: Phase II Bharat Atta at ₹30/kg MRP and Bharat Rice at ₹34/kg in 5 kg and 10 kg packs through NAFED/NCCF/Kendriya Bhandar now anchor the economy tier and compress branded-economy atta margins.

Premiumisation plus the shift off loose chakki flour: consumers are trading up to branded, packaged atta on hygiene and consistency, and the ₹/kg spread between economy (~₹30-38) and premium Sharbati (~₹60-85) has widened to roughly 2-3x on the same shelf.

Q-commerce habits reached small-town and semi-rural buying: grocery & staples is ~61% of India's quick-commerce mix (market ~USD 3.65 bn in 2026), which has trained buyers to expect 1 kg/2 kg top-up packs of atta, rice and poha alongside the monthly 10 kg bag.
Low-GI / diabetic-positioned staples emerged as their own price tier — sugar-release-control attas and diabetic-marketed rice brands now sell at a 40-100% premium to plain equivalents.

Packaged baby porridge flours (sprouted ragi, multigrain sathu maavu) moved from a DIY home preparation to a branded retail SKU set — Slurrp Farm, Manna, The Millet Store, Mighty Grains, Healthy Panda — with sprouted-and-roasted processing as the stated differentiator.
adjacentServices: In-store chakki / grind-on-demand: sell sabut gehun, maize, millets and jau and grind fresh to order — 15-30% margin against 3-8% on branded packs, and it solves flour shelf life in an 80%+ humidity monsoon instead of fighting it
Own-label repack of loose grain and flour into 1/2/5 kg bags (needs FSSAI licence plus Legal Metrology declarations and a verified scale)
Monthly staple standing order for staff-quarter families: fixed basket (atta, rice, sooji, besan, poha, dalia) delivered on salary date — kills the off-campus town trip that leaks the whole basket
Institutional / bulk indent counter for the school mess, two canteens and langar: 25-30 kg atta and 25-26 kg rice on quotation, priced separately from retail

Pre-book counter ahead of Navratri and Gurpurabs for fasting flours (kuttu, singhara, rajgira, samak, sabudana) and karah-prasad bundles (atta + sooji + ghee + sugar) — season prices move 15-35% and catering orders can double
Grain cleaning, sifting and winnowing service, plus airtight storage tins, food-grade drums and neem/bay-leaf pest sachets sold as an attachment to every bulk grain sale
Whole-grain buffer stocking as a monsoon/landslide service: hold grain and rice (which keep) rather than flour (which does not), and convert on demand via the chakki
Free intra-township home delivery of heavy 10 kg / 25 kg packs to staff quarters and hostels — the one thing q-commerce cannot reach here
Baby-food corner: sprouted ragi and sathu maavu with date-checked stock and a reorder reminder for parents of under-twos — a captive two-year subscription in practice
